title: FIS 102 - Aquatic Ecosystems and Fisheries Management

items.q: Which term is described by “the equipment that is used to capture fish from a water body”?
o: hook and line
fishing gear
cast net
gill net
items.s: fishing gear is the equipment that is used to capture fish from a water body.

items.q: freezing may be defined as
o: a salt tolerant tree that grows along sheltered tropical shores
the shallow edge of a lake where light reaches the bottom
all the fish of a stock that were produced in the same season
the storage of fish at very low temperature to stop bacterial growth
items.s: freezing: the storage of fish at very low temperature to stop bacterial growth. The other options describe year class, littoral zone, mangrove.

items.q: recruitment may be defined as
o: the entry of young fish into the part of the stock that can be caught
a young fish of a few weeks old that is ready for stocking
flowing water such as that found in a river or stream
a small narrow body of flowing water that feeds a river
items.s: recruitment: the entry of young fish into the part of the stock that can be caught. The other options describe fingerling, lotic water, stream.

items.q: Which of the following best describes smoking?
o: the use of smoke and heat from a fire to dry and flavour fish
a narrow tidal channel of water in the coastal mangrove belt
the treatment of fish so that it keeps for a long time without decay
the feeding position that an organism occupies in a food chain
items.s: smoking: the use of smoke and heat from a fire to dry and flavour fish. The other options describe preservation, creek, trophic level.

items.q: estuary may be defined as
o: a community of organisms and their water environment acting together
the lower end of a river where fresh and salt water mix
the tiny plants and animals that drift passively in the water
a large body of still water held in a hollow of the land
items.s: estuary: the lower end of a river where fresh and salt water mix. The other options describe plankton, aquatic ecosystem, lake.

items.q: Which term is described by “the network of feeding links that joins many food chains together”?
o: food chain
benthos
zooplankton
food web
items.s: food web is the network of feeding links that joins many food chains together.

items.q: brackish water may be defined as

the volume of water that a river carries past a point
the part of a river nearer its source where the current is faster
water of moderate salt content where a river meets the sea
items.s: brackish water: water of moderate salt content where a river meets the sea. The other options describe river discharge, upstream, benthos.

items.q: The statement “the microscopic green plants that float in water and make food” describes which of the following?

phytoplankton
benthos
trophic level
items.s: phytoplankton is the microscopic green plants that float in water and make food.

items.q: The statement “the largest population that a water body can support without damage” describes which of the following?

growth overfishing
population

items.s: carrying capacity is the largest population that a water body can support without damage.

items.q: Which of the following best describes riparian vegetation?

the rate at which fish are lost from a stock through death or capture

a shallow coastal water body separated from the sea by a sand bar
items.s: riparian vegetation: the plants growing along the bank of a river or stream. The other options describe mortality, lotic water, lagoon.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines trophic level?

items.q: reservoir may be defined as

a small narrow body of flowing water that feeds a river

items.s: reservoir: an artificial lake formed behind a dam for storing water. The other options describe cold chain, aquatic ecosystem, stream.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines population?
o: a series of organisms in which each one feeds on the one before it
the group of fish of one species living in a defined area

the open upper layer of a lake away from the bottom and the shore
items.s: population: the group of fish of one species living in a defined area. The other options describe pelagic zone, food chain, marine ecosystem.
